title: Senior asks: delete() first checks that the file is .csv or .json. Why not just call unlink()?
options: So the API can not delete other files in storage/, like .gitkeep or a .htaccess
Because unlink() works only for CSV and JSON
To make delete faster
The OS needs the extension to delete
explain: The API is for CSV and JSON files only. If delete accepts any name in storage/, a client can remove other files that live there. A short allow-list is a simple guard. basename() already stops ../ paths, the extension check limits the rest.

title: Senior asks: .vscode/launch.json is committed, but storage/ is not ignored. What is the better habit?
options: Ignore personal editor files, commit only what the whole team needs on purpose
Commit everything, git can handle it
Never use a debugger
Delete launch.json after every commit
explain: Editor files can hold local paths and ports and cause noisy diffs. Teams sometimes share one clean config on purpose. Decide it and write it in .gitignore. Also add storage/ uploads there, or git status is full of test files.

title: Senior asks: your first commits are called 'v-1' and '+debuger'. What message is better?
options: Add FileNameResolver so uploads do not overwrite files
fix
update all files
explain: A good message says what changed and why, in one short line, in the imperative: 'Add ...', 'Fix ...'. In half a year, git log is the only story of the project. 'v-1' and 'fix' tell nothing.

title: Senior asks: there are no tests for upload and FileNameResolver. Which one do you write first, and why?
options: FileNameResolver: it has file system races and a loop, so bugs hide there
The getters, they are easy
The jQuery code, there is no PHP in it
None: tests must not touch files
explain: Test where the risk is. The resolver creates files with fopen('x') and counts name, name_1, name_2. Write a test with a temp folder: free name, taken name, many taken names. Then add the upload test. Simple getters can wait.

title: PHP 8. What does this print?
explain: % in PHP keeps the sign of the left number: -7 % 3 = -1. intdiv cuts toward zero: -7 / 3 = -2.33 becomes -2 (not -3). The spaceship <=> gives -1, 0 or 1: 7 <=> 3 is 1. Use floor() when you want -3.

title: What does this print?
explain: A static property is stored once on the class that declares it. B extends A but does not redeclare $n, so A and B share the same variable. Three calls make it 3 in both. To get a separate counter, declare public static int $n again in B.

title: What does Node print?
explain: Sync code runs first: 1 and 4. Then the microtask queue (promise .then): 3. Last the timers (setTimeout, even with 0 ms): 2. Promise callbacks always go before setTimeout callbacks.

title: You changed app.php and created a new file notes.php (never added). You run git stash. What happens?
options: app.php is stashed, notes.php stays in the folder
Both files are stashed
Git refuses to stash
notes.php is deleted
explain: git stash saves only tracked changes by default. A new untracked file stays. Use git stash -u to include untracked files too. Check with git status after you stash.
